introduction: Schedules are basically appendices or lists at the end of the Constitution that categorize and tabulate bureaucratic activity and policy. The original Constitution in 1950 had only 8 Schedules. Four more were added through various amendments, bringing the total to 12 today.

core_concepts.title: First Schedule (1st)
core_concepts.description: Contains the list of names of all the States and Union Territories (UTs) of India, along with their territorial extent.

core_concepts.title: Eighth Schedule (8th)
core_concepts.description: Deals with the official 'Languages' recognized by the Constitution. Originally, it had 14 languages, but currently, it contains 22 official languages.

core_concepts.title: Tenth Schedule (10th)
core_concepts.description: Added by the 52nd Amendment Act (1985). It contains the 'Anti-Defection Law', which disqualifies MPs and MLAs who switch political parties after winning an election.

core_concepts.title: Schedules 11 and 12
core_concepts.description: 11th Schedule (added by 73rd Amendment) contains the powers, authority, and 29 functional items of 'Panchayats'. 12th Schedule (added by 74th Amendment) contains the powers and 18 functional items of 'Municipalities'.

important_entities.name: TEARS OF OLD PM
important_entities.significance: T-Territories(1), E-Emoluments(2), A-Affirmations/Oaths(3), R-Rajya Sabha seats(4), S-Scheduled Areas(5), O-Other Tribal Areas(6), F-Federal Lists(7), O-Official Languages(8), L-Land Reforms(9), D-Defection(10), P-Panchayats(11), M-Municipalities(12).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Because English is widely used for official work, students often assume it is in the 8th Schedule. It is NOT. 'English' is not among the 22 recognized languages in the 8th Schedule.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Schedule 2 is about Emoluments (Salaries), and Schedule 3 is about Oaths. Politicians always check the salary (2) before taking the oath (3)!

exam_strategy_tips: The simple fact that 'Originally there were 8 schedules, now there are 12' is a very common question in basic competitive exams (SSC, Railways).
The 8th (Languages) and 10th (Anti-Defection) are historically the most frequently asked schedules.
